title: Remembering vs Recognizing
hook: Learn the crucial difference that changes how you study.
cta: Try a 10-minute recall after this carousel

slides.label: Cover
slides.title: Remembering vs Recognizing
slides.body: One lets you reproduce knowledge; the other tells you it seems familiar. Which matters for real skills?
slides.callout: Which helps you actually use knowledge?

slides.label: Slide 2
slides.title: What is remembering?
slides.body: Active retrieval of facts or steps without cues. You reconstruct answers from memory.

slides.label: Slide 3
slides.title: What is recognizing?
slides.body: Identifying correct information when it's presented. Often based on familiarity, not full retrieval.

slides.label: Slide 4
slides.title: Why remembering helps more
slides.body: Retrieval strengthens memory, reveals gaps, and improves transfer to new problems.

slides.label: Slide 5
slides.title: When recognition is enough
slides.body: Quick scans, multiple-choice elimination, or initial exposure can use recognition efficiently.

slides.label: Final
slides.title: Final takeaway
slides.body: Train retrieval, not familiarity. Practice closed-book recall to make knowledge usable under pressure.
slides.footer: Discuss: How will you practice this?

caption: Quick practice (3 steps): 1) Read a paragraph. 2) Close the book and write everything you recall for 5–10 minutes. 3) Check errors, then repeat spaced sessions.
